title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Bound Logbook for the credit scoring console. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Bound Logbook
options.lineage: engineering lab logbooks — bound research notebooks with ruled entries, date stamps, and initialed sign-offs
options.thesis: Every score becomes a permanent, initialed record entry: the app is the lab notebook of a credit analyst, and every action leaves an entry.
options.viewport: The Predict screen as today's open page: printed header block (name, date, page), a side rail of colored page-edge tabs (Predict / Batch / SOP / Settings), and the work area as ruled record entries — each model run stamped, timed, initialed.
options.signature: THE LOG — every consequential action (prediction, memo verification, batch score, retrain) is appended as a stamped, initialed, timestamped entry; an applicant's file reads as the sequence of entries that produced it.
options.risk: Executed timidly it reads as a 'paper-themed SaaS'; the stamp / initials / entry ritual must be real interaction, not decoration.

raised.raise: Density courage: evidence modules pack edge to edge under hairline rules — no whitespace inflation.
Live binding: every what-if control drives an instantaneous, continuous re-score readout — no submit step.
One verdict, monumental: the decision band shows exactly one message, with the grade numeral at monumental scale.
The record balances on one sheet: the credit memo is one self-contained sheet carrying the complete record, printable as-is.
Every entry a nameplate: batch rows carry a compact identity plate and a one-line verdict note.

wireframe: │ ◉ AI CREDIT SCORING · LAB LOG    today 2026-10-06   pg. 04 │
│ ● THE LOG   │  14:33  model run · v7 · AUC 0.86 ... pn ✎   │

options.label: The Audit File
options.lineage: audit working papers and double-entry ledgers — tickmarks, reference codes, sign-off initials
options.thesis: The interface is an audit file: every claim is ticked and tied to its evidence; nothing enters the record without a reference.
options.viewport: Predict as working paper WP-01: an evidence index down the rail, ticked and referenced claims in the body (probability tied to model version, SHAP tied to exhibit, memo tied to its verification), and a tickmark legend with initials and date at the foot.
options.risk: The strongest grounded direction for this product — and the one most runs in this category land on; executed timidly it reads as generic enterprise software.
wireframe: │ AUDIT FILE — Credit Scoring   WP-01 · WP-02 · WP-03  ✓ PN  │
│ WP-03 SOP   │  memo claims 9/9 grounded ......... ✓ D-01   │
│ WP-04       │  SOP manual score 78 → B .......... ✓ E-07   │

options.label: High-Density Evidence Console
options.lineage: Japanese contemporary high-density web — boxed modules, hairline rules, utility-red tabs
options.thesis: The whole credit picture — probability, SHAP bars, memo status, drift alerts — packs into one hairline-ruled mosaic instead of a scrolling card stack.
options.viewport: A dense module mosaic: each job (score, factors, memo, log) is a small ruled box with its own tab, packed edge to edge; the decision banner is a red-tabbed module.
options.case: Fuses cleanly as a density play engineers respect; holds audience identification, loses narrowly on first-sight product clarity.
options.risk: At high density, scanability pays the price — one weak hierarchy decision and it becomes noise.
wireframe: │▓logo 予測 | バッチ | SOP | 設定          red-tab modules  │
││ A ✓ ││ what-if ││ demo  ││ entry entry entry entry entry │

options.label: Live-Bound Instrument
options.lineage: interactive type specimens — axis sliders morphing a grid live, monospace readouts
options.thesis: The what-if simulator becomes the hero: every slider bound live to an instantaneous re-score, the probability readout breathing in step.
options.viewport: Predict as an instrument: the score numeral enormous, what-if sliders as labeled axes, and every control mapped continuously to the readout — no submit button anywhere.
options.case: The what-if simulator maps perfectly onto live axis binding; as a whole world it carries less product clarity than the assigned direction.
options.risk: As a whole shell it can thin to one trick; the rest of the app must still read as a product.

options.label: Decision Signage
options.lineage: airport sign systems — saturated yellow bands, one message per band, monumental numbers, split-flap updates
options.thesis: A credit decision is wayfinding: one yellow band carries the single verdict, the grade numeral is monumental, and score updates flip like a departure board.
options.viewport: The Predict shell standard and clean; the decision banner is a hung yellow sign band with one message and a monumental grade; re-scoring animates a split-flap transition on the numerals.
options.case: Credit decisions really are wayfinding — the band and the split-flap update are memorable; overall shell is thinner than the assigned direction.
options.risk: A yellow-heavy shell can feel like signage rather than software if the world leaks past the decision band.
wireframe: │  Credit Scoring        Predict · Batch · SOP · Settings    │

options.case: Fuses poorly: hand-lettered whimsy undermines trust in a lending context.
